scope: Exact public initial/current implementation observations. No certificate is transferred to the historical paper run without an evaluated-revision bridge.

observations.claim: The repository parity script explicitly describes engine/omniscientist as the reference implementation used for paper experiments, while stating that engine, CLI skill, host skill and desktop are intentionally not fully identical and the parity script checks only invariants that must move together.
observations.interpretation: Edition parity is selective synchronization, not behavioral/certificate equivalence. A result certified under one entrypoint must not be inherited by another without a tested equivalence proof.

observations.claim: The public engine result-stage anti-fabrication predicate accepts when at least 60% of numeric tokens from key_numbers appear in the union of run_python stdout, provided the other result-stage checks pass; comments/prompts simultaneously instruct that every reported number must come from real output.
observations.scope_caution: This is a result-stage predicate over structured key_numbers, not proof that a final paper can contain arbitrary invented numbers. Other thesis/writeup/polish guards also exist. The finding is that the executable predicate is weaker than a literal all-key-numbers equality claim and must be described by its actual semantics.
observations.interpretation: Policy prose such as 'every number' is not itself an executable certificate; the gate revision and exact predicate must be bound to any claim about numerical traceability.

observations.claim: Public Git path history shows engine/omniscientist/agentic.py only at the parentless initial public commit, so the observed current engine predicate is the same public file lineage introduced on 2026-08-16; this still postdates arXiv submission and therefore is not historical run identity by chronology alone.
observations.interpretation: Stable public code after first publication does not close a pre-publication evaluated-source identity gap.

observations.claim: At the same initial public commit, cli/skills/omnisci/bin/gate_cli.py and skill/omnisci/bin/gate_cli.py are materially different implementations: the CLI copy hashes ledger entries/scripts, filters failed/stale records, verifies citations and uses a near-zero numeric epsilon, while the host-skill copy lacks those entry/script hashes and uses a 0.005 absolute grounding floor and different prose extraction behavior.
observations.interpretation: Both may implement anti-fabrication intent, but their acceptance languages differ. Host/CLI/engine certification must be edition-and-revision scoped.

handoff_rule.name: CLAIM_GATE_REVISION_AND_EDITION_BINDING
requirements: bind certification to exact executable gate revision/digest, not policy prose alone
do not transfer a pass between engine/host/CLI unless an explicit conformance suite proves the requested acceptance semantics
when publication predates first public source revision, keep evaluated-run attribution unresolved until a source bridge is supplied

relation_to_existing_protocols: Strengthens CLAIM_TO_EXECUTION_OUTPUT_SEMANTIC_BINDING and evaluator/reviewer revision scoping. It motivates a new evaluated-run source-revision binding gate but does not by itself establish a new performance effect.
